title: Empirical dequant cost sampler for kernel selection
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Dequantization and re-quantization overheads vary widely by layer shape, sequence length, micro-batch composition, and hardware (GPU architecture, memory bandwidth). Static heuristics that estimate a fixed dequant cost lead to suboptimal kernel choices: e.g., choosing an INT8-optimized attention kernel only to pay an unexpected dequant penalty that increases tail latency and token cost.

Goal: Add a lightweight empirical sampler and runtime telemetry hooks that measure per-model, per-layer dequant/quant overhead during normal traffic and use that data to drive the kernel selector and scheduling decisions. The sampler should be low-noise, safe for production, and designed to surface the crossover points between mixed-precision paths (INT8/FP8/FP16) so the kernel planner can pick the true lowest-latency/cost path for observed workloads.

Approach:
- Implement a sampling micro-benchmark integrated into the serving runtime that executes off-path microtrials for a small percentage of requests (configurable, default 0.5%). Each trial runs representative layer ops with the same tensor shapes and sequence lengths as the live request but in an isolated measurement context to avoid affecting KV cache or model state.
- Measured metrics: wall-clock dequant time, re-quant time, memory copy time (host<->device if applicable), additional kernel launch overhead, and intermediate memory pressure indicators. Tag measurements with model version, layer index/name, sequence length bucket, batch size, and selected kernel path.
- Feed measurements into an in-memory short-term aggregator and an asynchronous uploader to the metrics backend. Aggregates compute median/90/99th percentiles and estimated per-token cost delta for choosing alternate precision paths.
- Kernel selector integration: add a scoring component that combines static performance profiles with empirical delta from the sampler. Scoring respects latency SLOs and cost constraints; fallback logic prevents thrashing when sampler data is noisy.
- Safety and noise-control: start sampling in canary mode for new model versions, use exponentially-weighted moving averages (EWMA) per bucket, and require a minimum number of samples before changing kernel decisions for an active model/route.
- Config: runtime flags for sample rate, min_samples_threshold, bucket definitions, and a hard floor that prevents sampler-induced IQ adjustments under heavy load.

Deliverables:
- sampler runtime component + public config knobs
- metrics schema and dashboards (per-model/per-layer dequant cost)
- kernel selector extension that consumes sampler aggregates
- integration tests, perf benchmarks, and safety gating for rollouts
- migration/runbook for operators and SREs

Acceptance criteria:
- Sampler runs at default 0.5% with <1% increase to CPU utilization and negligible added p99 latency (<0.5ms observed on e2-standard test harness).
- For 3 internal benchmark models (small/med/large) sampler identifies at least one layer where empirical dequant cost changes the optimal kernel path compared to static heuristics.
- Kernel chooser uses sampler-derived adjustments to reduce average per-token latency or cost for those benchmarks by >=3% without increasing tail latency beyond SLO.
- Dashboards show per-layer median and p90 dequant/requant times within 24h of rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement sampler behind a feature flag and land unit tests (ENG-84512-1).
2) Canary on internal staging with sample_rate=5% for 48h; inspect dashboards and cold-start noise (ENG-84512-2).
3) Lower to production sample_rate=0.5% and enable uploader to metrics (ENG-84512-3).
4) Enable kernel-selector consumption in read-only mode (score visible in dashboards) for 72h (ENG-84512-4).
5) Allow automated adjustments subject to min_samples and EWMA thresholds (ENG-84512-5).

Testing strategy:
- Synthetic replay harness to feed controlled sequence lengths and batch sizes and validate sampler accuracy vs microbenchmarks.
- A/B test split traffic on a set of staging customers to verify benefits and regressions.
- Fault injection: simulate noisy GPUs / high memory pressure to validate sampler avoids unsafe decisions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: sampler trials could perturb scheduling or memory leading to regressions. Mitigation: isolate trials on spare CUDA streams and disallow sampler from allocating KV cache slices or touching persistent model buffers.
- Risk: noisy measurements lead to oscillation. Mitigation: EWMA + min_samples + hysteresis window before switching kernel paths.
- Risk: additional telemetry volume. Mitigation: sampling, aggregation, and compressed uplink; ability to disable uploader for air-gapped private deployments.

Out-of-scope: full cross-model offline autotuning sweep, persistent model-specific profiles stored long-term (may be a follow-up).
